Article Title: Oil prices dip marginally as US weighs easing sanctions on ‘shadow fleet’ tankers
Article Text:
Oil prices hold near $105 per barrel

Oil prices fell slightly on Friday as investors weighed rising tensions in the Middle East against the possibility of the US easing restrictions on ships carrying oil from sanctioned countries. Brent crude stood at $105.40, a decline of 0.52% while WTI crude was trading at $97.31, down 66 cents, or 0.67%.The dip came after a sharp rise in US crude prices during the previous session. WTI settled more than 3% higher on Thursday, supported by a significant reduction in US crude inventories. Brent, however, finished the session with little change.Efforts to increase supplies have also failed to fully ease market concerns. On Thursday, the International Energy Agency agreed to release more than 20 million barrels of diesel, alongside any oil left over from the record emergency reserve release announced in March. The move was intended to increase availability and bring down soaring prices.Another major factor under consideration is a possible change in US sanctions policy. The Trump administration is discussing whether to lift restrictions on certain vessels in the so-called “shadow fleet”, which has carried oil and petroleum products from Russia, Iran and Venezuela, a US official said on Wednesday, as cited by Reuters.The proposed step is aimed at easing record-high global freight rates.The deliberations follow US President Donald Trump’s temporary lifting of sanctions on Russian diesel fuel. The decision prompted criticism from Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy, European countries and some Republicans in the US Senate.Developments in the Middle East, meanwhile, continue to put pressure on the market. The intensifying conflict involving Saudi Arabia and Yemen’s Houthis, along with fresh attacks on ships in the region, has provided support to oil prices.Attacks around the waterway have increased over the past 10 days. Iran has said it is intensifying strikes in response to the US blockade of its ports and stricter sanctions imposed last month.The violence also spread to Yemen’s southern city of Aden on Thursday, when the Houthis fired missiles at the presidential palace complex, killing two guards. Separately, the Saudi-led coalition in Yemen reported dozens of attacks on Saudi infrastructure as the conflict continued to escalate.
Article Summary: Brent crude was trading at $105.40 per barrel on Friday, a decline of 0.52%. WTI crude was at $97.31, down 66 cents, or 0.67%. The dip came after a sharp rise in US crude prices during the previous session. Developments in the Middle East, meanwhile, continue to put pressure on the market.

Article Title: India raises petrol export duty fivefold to Rs 2.5/litre, cuts diesel levy to Rs 8.5
Article Text:
Govt raises petrol export duty, cuts diesel levy

NEW DELHI: The government has raised the export duty on petrol fivefold to Rs 2.5 per litre from Rs 0.5, while cutting the levy on diesel to Rs 8.5 per litre from Rs 16. The revised rates came into effect on October 16.The export duty on aviation turbine fuel (ATF) remains unchanged at Rs 10.5 per litre, according to a finance ministry notification issued on Friday.The revised rates cover the Special Additional Excise Duty (SAED), with no road and infrastructure cess (RIC) applicable on exports of petrol, diesel and ATF. The changes follow the previous revision, which took effect on October 1.Export duties on the three petroleum products are reviewed every fortnight, with rates determined by average international prices of crude oil and the respective fuels during the period since the last review. The latest revision changes the levies on petrol and diesel in opposite directions, while leaving the ATF duty unchanged.The revised export duties will not affect the existing excise duty rates on petrol and diesel sold for domestic consumption.India initially introduced windfall taxes on fuel exports in July 2022, before withdrawing them two years later. The government brought the levy back in March 2026 as crude oil prices surged during the US-Israeli war on Iran.The tax was intended to discourage exports and protect domestic supplies of petroleum products amid the conflict in the Middle East. It was also aimed at preventing exporters from benefiting unduly from differences between domestic and international prices as global crude oil prices rose.The government imposed export duties on diesel and ATF on March 27, 2026, and introduced the levy on petrol exports from May 16. Rates have since been reviewed every fortnight.
Article Summary: The export duty on aviation turbine fuel (ATF) remains unchanged at Rs 10.5 per litre. India initially introduced windfall taxes on fuel exports in July 2022, before withdrawing them two years later. The government brought the levy back in March 2026.

Article Title: India-China trade jumps 29% to $91.76 billion, overtakes US in first half of FY27
Article Text:
Representative image (India-China trade rebounds as New Delhi looks to rebuild bilateral ties)

India-US trade rises, but surplus narrows

India looks to rebuild trade ties with China

Exports rise across markets in first half of FY27

India’s bilateral trade with China rose nearly 29 per cent year-on-year to $91.76 billion in April-September 2026-27, making Beijing India’s largest trading partner in the first half of the financial year, according to commerce ministry data.Two-way trade between India and China stood at $71.24 billion in the corresponding period of 2025-26.China moved ahead of the US, with India’s trade with Washington rising 16.5 per cent to $83.14 billion during the first six months of the current fiscal year, compared with $71.39 billion a year earlier.India’s exports to China increased 36 per cent to $11.41 billion during April-September, from $8.38 billion in the year-ago period. Imports from China grew 27.82 per cent to $80.34 billion, against $62.86 billion previously.The faster growth in imports widened India’s trade deficit with China to $68.93 billion in the first half of FY27, from $54.06 billion in the corresponding period last year, the data showed.India’s bilateral trade with the US increased to $83.14 billion in April-September 2026-27 from $71.39 billion in the year-ago period.Exports to the US rose 11.11 per cent to $50.81 billion from $45.73 billion, while imports increased 25.98 per cent to $32.32 billion from $25.66 billion, according to the commerce ministry data.As imports grew faster than exports, India’s trade surplus with the US narrowed to $18.49 billion from $20.07 billion in the first half of 2025-26.Despite tariff-related disruptions, the US remained India’s largest merchandise export destination during the period. Commerce secretary Rajesh Agrawal said negotiations for the proposed India-US trade agreement were progressing in the right direction and that both sides were working to conclude it at the earliest.“The negotiations are in the right direction. Probably, we are in a very good zone. We anticipate closing the deal and signing it at the earliest possible time,” Agrawal said.He said the agreement would depend on the finalisation of the broader US tariff framework, with a parallel process underway under Section 301. India is seeking preferential access to the American market to help its exporters compete with those from other countries, he added.The increase in trade with China comes as New Delhi signals efforts to improve bilateral relations. Commerce and industry minister Piyush Goyal said on Wednesday that India was working to rebuild its relationship with China, but the last word on the process had not yet been scripted.Commerce secretary Rajesh Agrawal also said the two countries were in contact on trade-related issues.“There are discussions going on on both sides on trade issues also...constant discussions will help improve the trade ties between the two countries,” he told reporters, according to news agency PTI.The commerce ministry data also showed substantial changes in India’s trade with other countries during April-September 2026-27.Exports to Singapore rose 103 per cent, while shipments to Tanzania increased 122.5 per cent. However, exports to the UAE, the Netherlands and Saudi Arabia declined.On the imports side, inbound shipments from Oman rose 210.9 per cent, while imports from Brazil increased sharply, with the data citing a rise of 143.13 per cent. Imports from the UAE, Saudi Arabia and Switzerland declined.Separately, India’s merchandise exports rose 23.04 per cent year-on-year to $44.4 billion in September, while imports increased 8 per cent to $74.61 billion, according to government data.The merchandise trade deficit narrowed to $30.21 billion in September from $33 billion a year earlier, although it widened from $26.86 billion in August.Cumulatively, merchandise exports rose 18.51 per cent to $259.89 billion during April-September 2026-27, while imports increased 16.31 per cent to $437.53 billion. The trade deficit for the first half of the fiscal year widened to $177.64 billion from $156.88 billion in the corresponding period of 2025-26.Agrawal said exports were maintaining their growth trend and expressed hope that merchandise exports could exceed $500 billion if the momentum continued. India’s merchandise exports stood at $442 billion in 2025-26.
Article Summary: Bilateral trade with China rose nearly 29 per cent year-on-year to $91.76 billion. India’s exports to China increased 36 per cent to $11.41 billion during April-September, from $8.38 billion in the year-ago period.

Article Title: Elon Musk's monopoly charge, Reliance's response: What's the Starlink-Jio row all about?
Article Text:
Mukesh Ambani owned Reliance responds to allegations involving Musk's Starlink

Musk accuses Reliance of opposing Starlink’s entry

Government asks Starlink to comply with law

NEW DELHI: Reliance Industries has welcomed Elon Musk ’s Starlink to India, saying it has never feared competition and that its own satellite services are also in the queue.The statement comes as a response to Musk’s repeated allegations that vested interests were obstructing Starlink’s entry into India. Reliance, however, stressed that all companies must comply with Indian laws and regulations, adding that priority is to serve the people.In a statement released on Friday, the company said India’s investment and innovation landscape was open to both domestic and foreign players, with the same regulatory process applying to all applicants.The statement, posted on social media platform X, stated, “In light of recent remarks about Reliance and the Indian market, we wish to place the facts on record. Like every Indian enterprise, Reliance has grown in an India that welcomes investment and innovation, homegrown or international, that improve the lives of the people. That openness rests on the rule of law. As the Government of India has stated, it applies the same process to every applicant, Indian or foreign. Jio 's own satellite services await clearances.”The telecom firm further added, “At Reliance, we have never feared competition.We see it as the truest test of who serves the customer best. Jio itself entered India's crowded telecom market in 2016 as the newest player, with not a single customer. In just ten years, Jio has earned the trust of over 530 million customers and given Indians some of the best digital infrastructure and most affordable data in the world. We welcome competition in satellite communications, including Starlink. Every player, Jio included, must serve the people of India and abide by the laws and policies of the land.”Reliance’s statement came after SpaceX chief executive Elon Musk accused the Indian conglomerate of benefiting from the existing market structure and alleged that arguments against Starlink’s entry were contradictory.In a post on X, Musk had said, "The ridiculous arguments by Ambani’s army of Internet shills make no sense. On the one hand, they say Starlink couldn’t possibly compete with the amazing low prices offered by Ambani’s de facto monopoly in India and then, in the same breath, they essentially claim that Starlink would be too strong of a competitor! This is absurd hypocrisy and hyperbole."Musk argued that greater competition would give Indian consumers more choices, even if it reduced the profits of existing players. However, he said, this would not necessarily threaten their businesses."The reality is that competition would greatly benefit the average citizen in India by giving them more choices, as it always does. Ambani’s profits will be lower, but he is not going out of business," he wrote.Musk had previously alleged monopolistic practices in India’s telecommunications market and questioned the regulatory barriers facing Starlink’s commercial launch in the country.In another post, he directly addressed the government, writing, "Dear Prime Minister Ambani, Please accept my humble apologies for not realizing that you are the real boss of India. Naturally, you would prefer to maintain your monopolistic exploitation of the great people of India, but would you nonetheless consider allowing Starlink to compete?"The government has denied Musk’s allegation that Starlink was being discriminated against at the instance of a “local oligarch”.Union communications minister Jyotiraditya Scindia has said that there is no question of allowing a monopoly in satellite communications. He also said three entities are in line for final approval for commercial licences.Scindia said that India was close to taking a final decision on the pricing framework for satellite communication services. All licensed operators, including Starlink, must meet security requirements before beginning commercial operations.Starlink is yet to receive clearance to launch its services in India because it has not agreed to comply with regulations requiring satellite internet providers to establish domestic infrastructure, a senior government official said earlier this week.The government has no objection to the company rolling out its services once it addresses security concerns and agrees to establish local base stations, sources said.A base station is a radio transmitter and receiver that acts as a local hub, or the “first hop”, connecting end-user devices to a wireless network. The requirement to establish base stations is intended to help authorities ensure compliance with the law.Reliance Jio, Sunil Bharti Mittal-backed Eutelsat OneWeb and Musk’s Starlink are the three entities planning to launch satellite communication services in India.Bharti Enterprises chairperson Sunil Bharti Mittal has also said that Airtel’s satellite venture, Eutelsat OneWeb, could receive regulatory approval before Starlink because it applied earlier and is further along in the process.
Article Summary: Mukesh Ambani owned Reliance responds to allegations involving Musk's Starlink. Musk accuses Reliance of opposing Starlink’s entry into India. Reliance, however, stressed that all companies must comply with Indian laws and regulations, adding that priority is to serve the people.

Article Title: Rs 1 crore-plus salaries: Amid layoffs, which Indian IT sector jobs are getting huge salary premiums?
Article Text:
Even as restructuring and layoffs happen, some jobs in the IT sector are getting paid well - and across levels whether entry or senior.

Even as restructuring and layoffs happen, some jobs in the IT sector are getting paid well - and across levels whether entry or senior. Which roles are in demand? What are the average salary levels for special capability sets and which roles are under pressure?

What are the salary levels for those getting hired at premiums?

AI’s Role Disruption Map

Entry level salaries

The report lists annual salaries of Rs 1.08 crore for AI Architects, Rs 1.02 crore for Industrial Data Architects and Rs 95.8 lakh for OT Security Architects. These figures reflect the value that is being placed on designing, securing and governing complex technology systems, beyond coding alone.

Entry-level salaries for Tier 2 AI-Adjacent

Entry level salaries for Tier 3 AI-Support

So, what can IT sector professionals do?

At the entry level, he says professionals with strong foundations in software engineering, data and AI application can distinguish themselves through practical implementation skills.

At the mid-career level, expertise in areas such as AI engineering, machine learning operations and enterprise AI integration becomes particularly valuable as organisations look to move beyond experimentation towards deployment at scale.

At the senior level, compensation increasingly reflects the ability to architect enterprise AI systems, lead transformation programmes and ensure that technology investments deliver measurable business outcomes, he adds.

Early and Mid Career Salary Trends Across Roles

Biggest takeaway

For early-career professionals, this means building strong technical fundamentals while gaining hands-on experience in AI, data and cloud technologies.

For mid-career professionals, the priority is to move beyond execution and develop the ability to integrate technologies, improve workflows and translate domain expertise into scalable solutions.

For senior professionals, the focus must extend to strategic decision-making, enterprise-wide AI adoption, governance and the ability to connect technology investments with business performance, he says.

AI capability maturity framework: From skills to salary premiums

Till a few years ago, software engineers in India were commanding high salary premiums and the IT sector was a reliable source of employment. While still employing lakhs, the artificial intelligence-led disruptions have meant that there is growing uncertainty on the relevance of traditional IT sector roles.As Neeti Sharma, CEO of TeamLease Digital says, “Every few years, the labour market crosses a threshold that is easy to miss in the moment and impossible to reverse in hindsight. India's digital workforce crossed one this year.”“This landscape brings immense opportunity, but it also collapses old certainties about how talent is valued. Job titles and role definitions are becoming less reliable indicators of capability or compensation,” she says.The fundamental point to understand is that India’s technology talent market is witnessing a shift towards skill-differentiated compensation; with specialised capabilities in AI, machine learning, cloud engineering and data science becoming increasingly valuable.According to a TeamLease Digital report on Digital Skills and Salary Primer FY2026-27, there is a widening pay gap in India’s technology sector, with premiums increasingly going to professionals who can build, integrate, secure and manage AI systems. Routine, execution-led roles are facing greater salary pressure, while specialised skills are becoming more valuable.The premium concentrates in four families, AI, Data, Cloud and Cybersecurity, and peaks where capability depth meets governance and scale.And, this divide is visible across AI skill tiers. For example, the report puts entry-level median pay for AI-core roles at Rs 13.2 lakh, compared with Rs 9-10.2 lakh for AI-adjacent roles and Rs 4.8-5.4 lakh for AI-support roles. The projected salary growth is 16-21% for AI-core, against 13-18% for AI-adjacent and 7-8% for AI-support.Not only that, the premiums also extend to architecture, data and cybersecurity. The report says that skills such as GenAI engineers, AI architects, ML platform and cloud security are the highest in demand.“The 108.6 LPA figure is the median for AI Architects with 15+ years in our analysis of 37,000 roles. It reflects a senior role, not a market-wide norm. The differentiator is the ability to own architecture, scale production systems, manage risk, and connect technical decisions to business outcomes,” explains Neeti Sharma, CEO of TeamLease Digital.Also, geographies no longer define premiums as much. For example, according to the report, a GenAI engineer in Indore earns around Rs 16.5 lakh per annum, and out-earns cybersecurity talent in Bengaluru that gets Rs 14.4 lakh.Milind Shah, Managing Director, Randstad Digital - India tells TOI that the compensation for niche AI roles can vary considerably depending on the depth of expertise, role complexity and business impact. On an average, talent with niche tech skills may command anywhere between a 10-25% premium.Why are these roles commanding a premium? It’s a mix of skill shortage and the roles themselves generating more business value that routine IT jobs no longer are.According to Neeti Sharma, only about 16% of India’s IT professionals hold AI skills, so the supply is thin. She explains that companies are not able to find people who can take AI from pilot to production and stand accountable for it.“But this is not wage inflation. The market is pricing roles whose output is the AI system itself, which makes them the hardest to substitute. Routine support keeps operations running, and that is the layer AI is compressing first. Employers are paying for scarcity, and for people who can own the outcome,” she tells TOI.Reskilling is central to the shift. The TeamLease report points to pathways such as moving testers into intelligent operations, analysts into decision intelligence, and mid-career professionals into platform, product, governance and architecture roles.Its broader message is that combining core technical expertise with AI skills, domain knowledge and business judgement will increasingly determine salary growth.Milind Shah shares strategies for every level:So, what does this mean for tech professionals? The biggest takeaway is that professionals need to shift from being defined by the roles they perform to the capabilities they bring to the business.“As AI becomes embedded across technology functions, the value of talent will increasingly depend on the ability to adapt, solve complex problems and apply emerging technologies to real-world business challenges,” Milind Shah says.For people who are in traditional IT sector roles, it’s important to understand that while the jobs are not disappearing, routine execution roles are reducing.Repetitive reporting, manual testing, basic operational support and rule-based processing face pressure as AI and automation reshape work. The report does not suggest that all these jobs will disappear; rather, salary growth may slow unless workers move towards higher-value responsibilities.“Those in repetitive reporting, manual testing, and basic support are most exposed. The route up is adjacency, not reinvention: a BI analyst into data engineering, a sysadmin into cloud, a QA or IAM specialist into security and governance. Pair one technical skill with deep sector knowledge, and keep proof of work that moves a business outcome,” Neeti Sharma says.Not only that, this shift also has implications for how professionals approach career development.So if you are planning to upskill to keep yourself relevant, understand that it should not be driven solely by the popularity of a technology or the prospect of a higher salary.“Instead, employees should identify the capabilities emerging as critical within their industry, understand how these capabilities address business needs and build demonstrable expertise through practical application,” Milind Shah advises.
Article Summary: India’s technology talent market is witnessing a shift towards skill- differentiated compensation. Specialised capabilities in AI, machine learning, cloud engineering and data science becoming increasingly valuable. Routine, execution-led roles are facing greater salary pressure, while specialised skills are becoming more valuable.

Article Title: Rupee gains 20 paise against US dollar as RBI support kicks in, greenback weakens
Article Text:
Rupee gains 20 paise against US dollar

NEW DELHI: Rupee began Friday on a strong note, gaining 20 paise from its previous close to 94.79 against the US dollar. The rise came as American currency weakened and the impact of the Reserve Bank of India's structural forex interventions supported the unit.The gains, however, remained limited amid elevated crude oil prices and a negative beginning at Dalal Street.In the interbank foreign exchange market, the rupee began the session at 94.75 before moving to 94.79. The gain follows Thursday's 18-paise appreciation, which took the currency to a closing level of 94.99 against the dollar.Anuj Choudhary, research analyst at Mirae Asset Sharekhan, told PTI, "Decline in dollar index and softening of US treasury yields also supported the rupee. However, a surge in crude oil prices capped sharp gains. On the data front, US PPI (Producer Price Index) was hotter than expected while retail sales topped forecast. Weekly unemployment claims were in line with expectations."The dollar index, which tracks the US currency against a basket of six currencies, fell 0.54% to 102. US Treasury yields also eased, providing support to rupee.Meanwhile in the commodity market Brent crude futures were trading 0.54% lower at $105.35 per barrel.Domestic equities remained under pressure in early trade.BSE Sensex opened 113 points down at 74,187, while NSE Nifty50 slipped 27.20 points to 22,967.15. However, both indices turned green later in the session, with Sensex gaining 400 points and Nifty50 topping 23,100.Adding to the market backdrop, Foreign Institutional Investors (FIIs) were net sellers of domestic equities worth Rs 5,285.37 crore on Thursday, exchange data showed.
Article Summary: Rupee began Friday on a strong note, gaining 20 paise from its previous close to 94.79. The rise came as American currency weakened and the impact of the Reserve Bank of India's structural forex interventions supported the unit. However, a surge in crude oil prices capped sharp gains.

Article Title: Tech Mahindra jumps 8%, IT firm adds Rs 11,000 crore to market cap after blockbuster Q2 earnings
Article Text:
Tech Mahindra jumps 8%

IT shares lift benchmarks, but oil prices remain a concern

Tech Mahindra shares raced ahead of the BSE Sensex pack on Friday, sprinting over 8%, to add around Rs 11,000 crore to its market value. The blockbuster gains came after the IT firm reported a 32.74% jump in consolidated net profit for the September quarter.Tech Mahindra, along with other IT stocks helped domestic equity benchmarks shake off a sluggish start.Around 12.30 pm, Tech Mahindra shares were trading 8.05% higher at Rs 1,781.50 on the BSE. On the NSE, the stock was up 7.87% at Rs 1,779.90, a gain of Rs 129.90. Following the rise, Tech Mahindra's market capitalisation increased by Rs 10,974.86 crore to Rs 1,72,895.16 crore.The company's consolidated net profit attributable to its owners rose 32.74% year on year to Rs 1,585.6 crore in the July-September quarter of FY27, compared with Rs 1,194.5 crore in the corresponding quarter last year. The improvement was supported by strong volume growth, cost savings and rupee depreciation.Revenue from operations grew 15.6% to Rs 16,180.2 crore during the quarter, against Rs 13,994.9 crore in Q2 FY26. Compared with the preceding quarter, net profit increased 8%, while revenue rose 3%.Alongside its earnings announcement, Tech Mahindra's board recommended a bonus issue in the ratio of 1:1 to mark the company's 40th anniversary.The proposal means shareholders will receive one additional share for every share they hold. The company said in a regulatory filing that the bonus shares are expected to be credited by December 15.The proposed issue will be the company's first in 11 years. Its previous bonus issue, also in the ratio of 1:1, was announced in March 2015.The rally in technology stocks helped the domestic market turn positive after a muted start on Friday. ADD INFOThe recovery followed a strong session on Thursday, when both benchmarks recorded their biggest single-day gains in four months. The previous session's advance came as a global sell-off in AI-linked stocks created room for value buying in domestic equities, alongside gains driven by individual companies' earnings."Markets are witnessing a sharp rebound, supported by a resurgence in IT stocks following strong quarterly results, even as other Asian markets plunged on a sell-off in AI-linked stocks," said Ankur Punj, managing director of Equirus Wealth.However, the advance remained constrained by concerns about elevated crude oil prices and rising US producer prices, which continued to keep global investors cautious. Domestic market participants were also tracking quarterly earnings, with stock-specific developments influencing trading, two analysts said.Brent crude was hovering around $105 per barrel on Friday.Of the 16 major sectors, 11 were trading higher. Small-cap and mid-cap stocks, which had declined during the early part of the session, were trading flat.The IT index rose 3%, with Tech Mahindra leading the advance after beating second-quarter revenue expectations on the back of robust deal wins. The positive sentiment extended to other major technology stocks, with Infosys trading nearly 4% higher, TCS gaining 3.26% and HCLTech rising more than 1%.Wipro shares advanced 5.7% after the company reported September-quarter revenue above expectations. Elsewhere, Reliance shares fell 0.3%, giving up some ground after gaining 3.4% in the previous session. The earlier advance had followed the announcement of pricing for the Jio Platforms IPO.HDFC Life declined 2% despite reporting higher quarterly profit. Some brokerages pointed to the company's subdued near-term outlook amid proposed distribution reforms, which overshadowed September-quarter earnings that were in line with expectations.
Article Summary: IT shares lift benchmarks, but oil prices remain a concern. Tech Mahindra shares raced ahead of the BSE Sensex pack on Friday, sprinting over 8%. The IT firm reported a 32.74% jump in consolidated net profit for the September quarter.

Article Title: Air India cancels all flights to and from three Saudi cities till October 20
Article Text:
Air India cancels all Saudi flights

How to get a refund for cancelled Air India flights

Website or app bookings: Visit Air India’s Manage Booking section to request a refund. Travel agent or third-party website bookings: Contact the agent or website to initiate the refund. Ticketing office bookings: Visit the same Air India office where you purchased the ticket to request a refund. Checking refund status: For bookings made and cancelled through Air India’s website or app, visit the refund support portal and select ‘Status Check on Pending Refund’. For other bookings, contact the respective agent, website or ticketing office. Refund credit: The amount will be credited to the account used to pay for the booking. If that account is closed or invalid, provide your new bank details to an Air India agent at the ticketing office.





More carriers halt Saudi services

Air India sets up team to cut costs

NEW DELHI: Air India has cancelled all flights to and from Riyadh, Dammam and Jeddah until October 20, as the situation in Saudi Arabia continues to evolve. The airline said that it is monitoring developments and assessing the situation to ensure flights could resume safely.“In view of the evolving situation in Saudi Arabia, all Air India flights to and from Riyadh, Dammam and Jeddah stand cancelled until 20 October 2026. We are closely monitoring developments and continuously assessing the situation to ensure the safe resumption of operations.”Referring to refunds due to the cancellation, the aviation giant said, “Passengers affected by these cancellations are being offered a full refund. At Air India, the safety and security of our passengers and crew remain the highest priority.”The latest cancellations follow flight disruptions announced last week, when Air India, Akasa Air and IndiGo suspended or reduced flights to Riyadh after reports of explosions, including a loud blast at the city's international airport.Passengers affected by the cancellations can request a refund by following these steps:Several other international airlines have also changed their schedules amid the conflict.Air France-KLM has extended the suspension of flights to and from Riyadh until the end of October. Akasa Air has suspended services to and from Jeddah and Riyadh until October 17, while IndiGo has cancelled flights to and from Riyadh, Jeddah, Dammam and Madinah until the same date.Etihad Airways has cancelled all flights between Abu Dhabi and Riyadh, along with 10 flights to Dammam and Jeddah, until October 19. Gulf Air has cancelled flights to and from Riyadh from October 12 to October 17, while Lufthansa Group airlines have cancelled all flights to Riyadh until October 16.Malaysia Airlines has cancelled flights to and from Jeddah and Madinah until October 17 as a precaution. Philippine Airlines has extended the suspension of its Riyadh flights until November 29, while Qatar Airways has temporarily suspended flights to and from Riyadh and Dammam.Other airlines have pushed back their plans to resume services. Cathay Pacific has postponed the resumption of its Hong Kong-Dubai and Hong Kong-Riyadh routes until January 31, 2027. Delta Air Lines has delayed its planned flights from Atlanta to Riyadh until March 2027.Meanwhile, Air India has set up a team to find ways to reduce costs across the airline as it faces rising operating pressures. Its new CEO, Tewolde Gebremariam, has asked employees to focus on spending carefully and taking responsibility for their work.In a message to staff on October 12, he said, "A multidisciplinary, cross-functional Cost Savings Team has been established on full-time basis to identify cost-saving opportunities across the organisation,"The team will review spending across departments and look for ways to save money, he said."Ongoing airspace closures, the conflict in the Middle East and its resulting operational disruptions, and persistently high jet fuel costs continue to place significant pressure on airlines across the industry," he said.Air India, jointly owned by the Tata Group and Singapore Airlines, reported a consolidated loss of Rs 22,238.23 crore in the 2025-26 financial year.Meanwhile, the Middle East conflict has now continued for more than seven months, keeping airlines and oil markets on edge.
Article Summary: Air India has cancelled all flights to and from Riyadh, Dammam and Jeddah until October 20. The airline said that it is monitoring developments and assessing the situation to ensure flights could resume safely. Air India has set up a team to find ways to reduce costs across the airline.

Article Title: FM Sitharaman seeks early India-US trade deal, flags China’s market access barriers
Article Text:
Finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman

BRICS should focus on people's welfare

Infrastructure spending has helped sustain India's growth

NEW DELHI: Finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman has called for an early conclusion of the India-US trade agreement, stressing its importance for bilateral economic relations and global trade.Her remarks come a day after commerce and industry minister Piyush Goyal said the first phase of the trade pact had been finalised and was currently undergoing legal drafting."I think recently the Indian commerce minister has also spoken that they expect and wish to have the agreement signed soon. Negotiations have been going on. I hope, in the interest of global trade and in the interest of trade between the two partners, India and US, the trade agreement gets concluded at the earliest," she said on Friday.FM Sitharaman also raised concerns over India's trade relationship with China, particularly the growing imbalance and the difficulties Indian businesses face in accessing the Chinese market.Despite years of engagement with Beijing, India has made little headway in securing greater market access for several products, including generic medicines, bovine meat, vegetables and other perishable goods, she said.Speaking to the Atlantic Council on the sidelines of the IMF-World Bank annual meetings in Bangkok, Thailand, the finance minister pointed to non-tariff restrictions as a key impediment to trade between the two countries."Non-tariff barriers are the biggest hurdle in the trade between India and China," she said. China had continued to use phytosanitary measures and other non-tariff restrictions, she added, despite the possibility of addressing these issues through discussions and investigations.Sitharaman said India had chosen negotiations over punitive tariffs as a means of tackling substantial trade imbalances with its trading partners, even if reaching a resolution took time.On BRICS, minister Sitharaman rejected the view that the grouping's purpose was to counter another country or bloc. Instead, she said, its focus should be on strengthening cooperation for the benefit of its people."I don't think BRICS's intention is to counter others. It is more to strengthen the partnership through the BRICS," she added.She highlighted the grouping's scale, noting that its member countries represented nearly 40 per cent of the world's population. Greater cooperation among them could support trade, improve mutual understanding and open up economic opportunities, she said.Sitharaman also pointed to the expanding membership of BRICS, with 11 to 12 countries actively engaging with one another and collectively accounting for around 45 per cent of global trade.Turning to the domestic economy, Sitharaman said India had maintained strong growth despite disruptions across the world. The country had been the fastest-growing major economy over the previous four to five years, particularly since the COVID-19 pandemic, she said.She credited this performance to a combination of inclusive growth, improved access to resources, skill development for young people, fiscal prudence and higher public capital expenditure.The finance minister emphasised the role of infrastructure investment in supporting economic activity, saying it had a stronger multiplier effect than directly transferring an equivalent amount of money to people. Such investment also generated employment, she said.According to Sitharaman, public expenditure on infrastructure allows money to reach people through the economic activity it creates, while avoiding the same degree of pressure on the fiscal deficit that some other forms of spending could entail.She also linked government borrowing to the creation of infrastructure assets, arguing that the approach had delivered economic benefits. "Borrowing goes for asset creation, and as a result, the economy has benefited," she said.
Article Summary: Finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman calls for early conclusion of the India-US trade agreement. She also raised concerns over India's trade relationship with China, particularly the growing imbalance and difficulties Indian businesses face in accessing the Chinese market. She rejected the view that the grouping's purpose was to counter another country.

Article Title: She received Rs 9.04 lakh leave encashment on retiring from LIC; taxman allowed only Rs 3 lakh exemption, but ITAT Jaipur grants relief even after 1,277-day appeal delay
Article Text:
The Income Tax Department restricted her exemption to Rs 3 lakh and sought to tax the balance of Rs 6.04 lakh. (Image for representative purpose only)

What the case is about

Why did the retired woman win relief?

Collector, Land Acquisition v. Mst Katiji

How much of your leave encashment is exempt from income tax? That depends on whether you are a government employee or a private sector employee. The limit for private sector employees was recently raised to Rs 25 lakh.In one case, a retired woman faced a tax notice on her leave encashment, with the Income Tax Department allowing only part of it for exemption. Read on to know why she won relief from ITAT.A woman retired from Life Insurance Corporation of India (LIC) on June 30, 2020 after more than 30 years of service. She received Rs 9.04 lakh as leave encashment, in addition to her other retirement benefits. While filing her income tax return (ITR), she claimed a tax exemption on the entire leave encashment amount.Also Read | Taxpayer declared Rs 1.79 lakh in ITR, faced Rs 11.22 crore income addition on large cash deposits, unsecured loans; ITAT grants him chance to substantiate case with condition he plant 500 trees She was unaware that LIC employees fall under the category of non-government employees for this purpose. Under the rules applicable in 2020, she was eligible for a tax exemption of only Rs 3 lakh on leave encashment, rather than the full Rs 9.04 lakh she had claimed. The exemption limit for leave encashment received by non-government employees was raised to Rs 25 lakh in Budget 2023.The Income Tax Department restricted her exemption to Rs 3 lakh and sought to tax the balance of Rs 6.04 lakh.This led to an income tax notice being issued to her.In her application seeking condonation of delay, the woman explained that she had entrusted the matter to a tax consultant. According to her, the consultant did not file the appeal before the tribunal or inform her that the Commissioner of Income Tax (Appeals) had dismissed her case. She said she learnt about the order after receiving a substantial tax demand.As a result, she approached the Income Tax Appellate Tribunal (ITAT), Jaipur, only after a delay of around 1,277 days, engaging a new chartered accountant to pursue the matter.The Income Tax Department opposed her request, arguing that she had not established “sufficient cause” for such a long delay.The tribunal first had to decide whether her explanation justified condoning the delay and then consider whether the higher exemption limit applied to her leave encashment.On September 28, 2026, Mrs Moongia won the case before the ITAT Jaipur.Also Read | Woman paid Rs 79 lakh for a Rs 2.14 crore villa, but construction remained unfinished; Telangana RERA orders full refund with 10.7% interest and fines builder Rs 1.03 crore The ITAT Jaipur accepted her request to condone the delay of 1,277 days. It observed that the law recognises that an individual should not be held responsible for a mistake or negligence committed by a tax consultant hired to handle their tax matters. A taxpayer should not have to suffer because of an error made by their consultant.On the delay, the tribunal considered Moongia's explanation that she had relied on her tax consultant to handle the proceedings. It observed that a professional handling a client's tax case was expected to communicate important developments, including the dismissal of an appeal, and advise the client on the next steps.The tribunal stated that “mistake or negligence on the part of a tax consultant engaged by the assessee cannot be attributed to the assessee and he/she should not be made to suffer.” It also referred to the Supreme Court's decision in, which supports a liberal approach to condoning delays in appropriate cases.Also Read | He moved to the US for a job and forgot to file his India ITR; taxman imposed Rs 8.29 lakh penalty, but ITAT Jaipur cancelled it for this reason After considering her explanation, the tribunal held that there was “sufficient cause” to condone the delay of 1,277 days. It therefore admitted the appeal for consideration on its merits.The tax dispute concerned the exemption ceiling under Section 10(10AA). The tax authorities had relied on the Rs 3 lakh limit, while the woman’s representative cited CBDT Notification No. 31/2023, dated May 24, 2023, which raised the exemption limit for eligible employees to Rs 25 lakh.The Jaipur tribunal also considered earlier ITAT decisions that had applied the revised limit. It noted that a coordinate bench had already ruled in favour of allowing leave encashment exemption within the Rs 25 lakh ceiling.Explaining its conclusion, the tribunal said: “In view of this legal position, we are in respectful agreement of what has been held by the afore cited coordinate Jaipur Benches of this Tribunal as noted hereinabove.”Also Read | She bought shares for Rs 13.5 lakh and sold them for Rs 77.47 lakh after 18 months; taxman denied capital gains exemption, but ITAT gives relief and deletes Rs 79 lakh in additions It ultimately held that the woman was eligible for exemption on the Rs 9,04,669 she had received.Chartered Accountant Suresh Surana told ET that leave encashment paid to central and state government employees upon retirement is completely exempt from income tax. However, employees working in the private sector and other non-government organisations are eligible for exemption only up to the limits laid down under the income-tax law.Surana said any leave encashment received beyond the eligible exemption limit is taxable under the head “salaries” in the year in which the payment is received. The excess amount is taxed at the normal income-tax slab rates applicable to the employee, with no separate or special tax rate for leave encashment.
Article Summary: A woman retired from Life Insurance Corporation of India (LIC) on June 30, 2020. She received Rs 9.04 lakh as leave encashment, in addition to her other retirement benefits. While filing her income tax return (ITR), she claimed a tax exemption on the entire amount. The Income Tax Department restricted her exemption to Rs 3 lakh and sought to tax the balance of Rs 6.04 crore.

Article Title: CERT-In issues 'critical' alert as AI agents access 'confidential' data of Indian firms'
Article Text:
CERT-In issues warning after AI agents accessed live systems and confidential data of organisations without authorisation

AI Agents

as Attack Vectors

AI tools speed up cyberattacks

What organisations should do

NEW DELHI: India’s cybersecurity agency CERT-In has issued a “critical” alert after autonomous artificial intelligence (AI) agents under test accessed live systems and confidential data belonging to Indian organisations without authorisation.The agency has also warned that cybercriminals are using publicly available AI tools to launch attacks faster, leaving businesses with only hours to respond.In an advisory titled, the Indian Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT-In) detailed two types of incidents affecting the country's organisations.In the first, AI model providers reported that AI models and agents being tested for research and evaluation had gone beyond their assigned tasks and accessed live systems.The agents were able to read business records containing personal information and confidential material by using credentials and connection settings exposed in application configurations, public code repositories and cloud services with excessive access permissions.A key concern was that none of the affected organisations detected the unauthorised access themselves. The incidents came to light only after the AI model providers disclosed them following internal reviews, CERT-In said as cited by news agency PTI.In a separate set of incidents identified through its own threat monitoring, CERT-In found cybercriminals using publicly available AI-based security tools to scan targets, identify weaknesses and exploit them in financially motivated attacks against Indian entities.These tools were being repackaged and deployed on servers across several countries, the agency said.According to CERT-In, the use of AI-powered tools reduced the time between gaining initial access to a system and causing damage from several days to just a few hours. Organisations that only partially fixed the security weaknesses were targeted again within days, with attacks carried out on a larger scale.The agency said the incidents stemmed from familiar security lapses that AI tools could identify and exploit faster and on a greater scale than human attackers.These included passwords, access keys and other credentials exposed in source code, public repositories, configuration files and web content; outdated or unused application programming interfaces (APIs) still accessible over the internet; payment API keys stored in plain text; and cloud services granting more permissions than necessary.Internet-facing administrative systems, outdated software and weak passwords or the absence of multi-factor authentication also created opportunities for attackers.In some incidents, AI agents retrieved the same exposed credentials again and reused them in separate operations, CERT-In noted.CERT-In has urged organisations to audit their source code, public repositories and their histories, configuration files, client applications and cloud storage to identify exposed credentials. Any compromised credentials should be changed, and sensitive information should be removed from code histories.The agency has also recommended shutting down unused or outdated APIs, limiting cloud access to only what is necessary, removing administrative interfaces from public internet access and enforcing multi-factor authentication.Organisations should monitor systems for suspicious activity and retain logs for at least 180 days.
Article Summary: India's cybersecurity agency CERT-In has issued a ‘critical’ alert after autonomous artificial intelligence (AI) agents under test accessed live systems and confidential data belonging to Indian organisations. The agency has also warned that cybercriminals are using publicly available AI tools to launch attacks faster.

Article Title: ‘Welcome competition in satcom, including Starlink’: Reliance Industries rebuts Musk's claims
Article Text:
Jio LEO satellite ground station model

NEW DELHI: Ahead of its upcoming mega Rs 30,213-crore Jio IPO, Mukesh Ambani’s Reliance Industries has rebutted Elon Musk ’s tirade on X. Last Wednesday, Musk had accused “certain oligarchs” of “blocking” Starlink’s entry to India without naming anyone but saying “you can guess who they are” and then named Ambani over the next two days in a series of X posts.On Friday, Reliance Industries said in a statement statement: “We welcome competition in satellite communications, including Starlink. Every player, Jio included, must serve the people of India and abide by the laws and policies of the land.”“At Reliance, we have never feared competition. We see it as the truest test of who serves the customer best. Jio itself entered India's crowded telecom market in 2016 as the newest player, with not a single customer. In just 10 years, Jio has earned the trust of over 53 crore customers and given Indians some of the best digital infrastructure and most affordable data in the world,” the statement said.Govt had also denied Musk’s charges. Last Thursday, Union telecom minister Jyotiraditya Scindia had said at the India Mobile Congress: “There is a lot of conversation about a particular party (Starlink). But there are three parties that have got licenses… As and when govt decides the charge system on revenue basis spectrum will be assigned to them and as and when they individually fulfil security conditions, then they can start operations.Sunil Bharti-backed Eutelsat OneWeb, Ambani’s Reliance Jio and Musk’s Starlink have got licences and are preparing to start satcom service here so that even remote areas where laying ground infra for broadband is not possible can get the same. Billionaire Jeff Bezos-led Amazon's Project Kuiper is eying a licence to do so.The Reliance statement issued Friday said: “Like every Indian enterprise, Reliance has grown in an India that welcomes investment and innovation, homegrown or international, that improve the lives of the people. That openness rests on the rule of law. As govt of India has stated, it applies the same process to every applicant, Indian or foreign. Jio's own satellite services await clearances.”
Article Summary: Mukesh Ambani’s Reliance Industries has rebutted Elon Musk ’s tirade on X. Musk had accused “certain oligarchs’ of “blocking” Starlink”“At Reliance, we have never feared competition,” the statement said.

Article Title: Wipro revenue edges up, deal bookings hit 4-year low
Article Text: BENGALURU: Wipro made a weak start to the second half of FY27, with flat sequential growth and total bookings falling to a near four-year low as deal signings were delayed. Client-specific issues in its mainstay market, Americas 1, and weakness in healthcare also weighed on performance.IT services revenue was flat sequentially and grew 0.6% year-on-year in constant currency in the Sept quarter. In dollar terms, revenue declined 0.1% sequentially and grew 0.3% YoY to $2.6 billion. Operating margin stood at 16.5%, expanding 50 basis points sequentially but declining 20 basis points YoY.Total bookings stood at $2.6 billion, down 22.9% sequentially in constant currency. Large-deal bookings fell 58.6% sequentially to $674 million. “Our bookings were lower this quarter. However, a couple of deals that had been awarded to us were not signed during the quarter. We expect these to flow into Q3, and we are very bullish about our Q3 bookings performance. There was a specific client-related situation in Americas 1, along with an issue in healthcare,” said Wipro CEO Srini Pallia. He said the company typically sees a significant impact from client furloughs in the Dec quarter but expressed confidence in its pipeline and deal momentum.Wipro does not disclose AI revenue separately. “We track these numbers internally but have not disclosed them externally. We want to avoid repeating what happened with digital services in the past. Our focus is on transforming clients through AI and helping them become AI-native,” Pallia said.
Article Summary: IT services revenue was flat sequentially and grew 0.6% year-on-year in constant currency. Operating margin stood at 16.5%, expanding 50 basis points sequentially but declining 20 basis points YoY. Total bookings stood at $2.6 billion, down 22.9% sequentially.

Article Title: CAS tweaked, change in F&O settlement rules
Article Text: MUMBAI: Markets regulator Sebi on Thursday revised the process for Closing Auction Session (CAS) that included changing the trading timings and how the settlement prices of stocks and indices would be arrived at for derivatives contracts, a Sebi circular said.Under the changed rules, there will be a 10-minute CAS that will start at 3:30 pm and end at 3:40 pm on all trading days. At the same time, trading in index and stock derivatives will continue until 3:45 pm, except for index derivatives contracts on the expiry day.Sebi also brought in a major change relating to how the settlement prices of expiring derivatives contracts are calculated. This will now be based on a Volume Weighted Average Price (VWAP) methodology using the last 30 minutes of continuous trading.Order entry for both limit and market orders will be allowed from 3:31 pm to 3:36 pm, followed by a period during which only limit orders can be placed. The session will close randomly between 3:38 pm and 3:40 pm.The post-close session in the cash segment will run from 3:50 pm to 4 pm, with trades executed at the closing prices of securities.Earlier, since the introduction of CAS in Aug, this was based on prices arrived through the CAS process.After CAS was enforced, during several sessions, wild swings in index levels and stock prices were seen.After this, and also after Sebi’s investigations found some brokers were manipulating the system, the regulator issued another consultation paper.Post that, Sebi also had discussions with its Secondary Market Advisory Committee and with the stock exchanges. It also went through the several thousand comments it received on its proposals. Sebi introduced CAS in India with the objective of improving transparency and price discovery while ensuring a more orderly closing process.The new changes would be implemented in two phases, between Dec 7 and Feb 8, 2027, the Sebi release said
Article Summary: Sebi also brought in a major change relating to how the settlement prices of expiring derivatives contracts are calculated. This will now be based on a Volume Weighted Average Price (VWAP) methodology using the last 30 minutes of continuous trading. The new changes would be implemented in two phases, between Dec 7 and Feb 8, 2027.

Article Title: Facing headwinds, Air India sharpens cost control focus
Article Text:
Air India is forming a dedicated team to identify cost-saving opportunities in operations while facing significant challenges.

NEW DELHI: Air India MD and CEO Tewolde Gebremariam has set up a “multidisciplinary, cross-functional cost savings team” to find all possible ways and means of reducing expenditure on “full-time basis” amid mounting losses. Air India reported a loss of about $2.3 billion in 2025-26, the biggest annual loss since the Tata Group acquired the airline along with AI Express in Jan 2022. Overall, since then the airline has lost about $5.7 billion due to a combination of both internal and external factors.“While many external factors remain beyond our control, how we manage costs is something each of us can influence every day. Cost saving… requires active participation and commitment of every employee… Alongside operational excellence, we need to embed a mindset of frugality, accountability, and thoughtful decision-making in everything we do. We should continually challenge ourselves to ask – is this expenditure necessary? Is there a more efficient way to achieve the same outcome? Small decisions, taken consistently across organisation, can collectively strengthen financial resilience,” said Tewolde.While airlines globally have been facing elevated oil prices since the West Asia crisis along with other geopolitical challenges, Indian carriers have been worse off due to the rupee crashing and Pakistan airspace closure only for them.For Air India, the situation is even worse post the deadly Ahmedabad crash last June.“…a multidisciplinary, cross-functional cost saving team has been established on full-time basis to identify cost-saving opportunities across the organisation. They will systematically review all expenditure and identify cost-saving opportunities across functions,” his memo says.
Article Summary: Air India reported a loss of about $2.3 billion in 2025-26, the biggest annual loss since the Tata Group acquired the airline along with AI Express. Overall, since then the airline has lost about $5.7 billion due to a combination of both internal and external factors.

Article Title: 'Mistry's tenure over, no basis to challenge Trusts' functioning'
Article Text:
Mistry responded with a submission on Thursday, asking Bai Hirabai to file an affidavit stating that Noel Tata met the eligibility criteria.

MUMBAI: Mehli Mistry has no standing to challenge how two Tata trusts are run, the trusts told the charity commissioner's office on Thursday. Sir Dorabji Tata Trust (SDTT) and Bai Hirabai Jamestji Tata Navsari Charitable Institution said Mistry's trusteeship tenure ended on Oct 28 last year, so he could not use it to challenge their administration and governance.In its affidavit, Bai Hirabai disputed Mistry's reading of Clauses 6 and 18 of its Trust Deed, which set eligibility for trusteeship by religion and residence. It argued that these restrictions conflict with the original Will and Codicil governing the Trust and should not be given effect. Bai Hirabai also filed a substitution application to name Noel Tata as reporting trustee in the matter related to Mistry's complaints on the trust's affairs, after Vijay Singh ceased to be a trustee earlier this year.Mistry responded with a submission on Thursday, asking Bai Hirabai to file an affidavit stating that Noel Tata met the eligibility criteria."It is submitted that the deputy Charity Commissioner shall ensure that the reporting trustee (Noel) proposed to be substituted by way of the present application shall be a qualified Trustee as contemplated in Clauses 6 and 18 of the Trust Deed dated Dec 7, 1923, which inter alia states that trustee shall be a Parsi professing Zoroastrian religion," Mistry said in his submission.Mistry claimed that Bai Hirabai's board included trustees who were ineligible because they did not meet the criteria in the trust deed, which required a trustee to be a permanent resident of Mumbai or Navsari and to belong to the Zoroastrian Parsi faith. In a separate hearing, the Sir Ratan Tata Trust (SRTT) also told the charity commissioner that the office's May 15 order, which bars it from holding any meetings, created challenges for its functioning.
Article Summary: Sir Dorabji Tata Trust (SDTT) and Bai Hirabai Jamestji Tata Navsari Charitable Institution said Mistry's trusteeship tenure ended on Oct 28 last year. Mistry responded with a submission on Thursday, asking Bai Hira to file an affidavit stating that Noel Tata met the eligibility criteria.

Article Title: Irdai looking at ways to help policyholders stay the course
Article Text: MUMBAI: Irdai is exploring ways to finance life insurance premiums against policy surrender values to help policyholders avoid premature surrenders and retain policies until maturity, chairman Ajay Seth said at Samvaad 2026, organised by Sahamati, the self-regulatory organisation for account aggregators.Many policyholders surrender policies when they need money or face a temporary income shortfall, particularly those outside the salaried workforce. Financing the final few premium instalments could help them retain the policy and realise better value at maturity, while giving lenders an existing policy value as security. "A significant number of policyholders surrender their policies because they need money. Another situation arises when income varies, particularly among people who are not salaried," Seth said. "Financing those final instalments could be useful. If the premiums are paid over time, the policyholder can realise better value, while the lender has an embedded value to rely on."Seth said a grey market had emerged for policy assignments, which he said were not permitted under the Insurance Act. "We could develop a formal channel for premium financing instead," he said. Irdai is also examining financing for health insurance premiums, which can be difficult for households with limited monthly incomes to pay upfront.
Article Summary: Irdai exploring ways to finance life insurance premiums against policy surrender values. Many policyholders surrender policies when they need money or face a temporary income shortfall. Financing the final few premium instalments could help them retain the policy and realise better value at maturity.

Article Title: Naga-Kuki clashes in Manipur: Kuki woman killed in Kamjong, severed head of Naga man found in Kangpokpi
Article Text:
Kuki-Zo woman, was killed in an ambush by suspected Naga militants, severed head of Naga man found

Poll Vote & Share your view What do you think is the most important step to reduce ethnic violence in Manipur? Dialogue between the communities Stronger security measures Greater efforts by the government Community-led peace initiatives 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion





GUWAHATI: A Kuki-Zo woman was killed and her husband injured in an alleged ambush by suspected Naga militants in Manipur’s Kamjong district on Thursday, while two other members of the community were reported missing as ethnic violence continued in the state.The deceased, Hatneikim Haokip, was from Molnoi village.Preliminary information suggests the group was travelling to Phaikoh to buy essential commodities when they were ambushed on the road between Phaikoh and Aishu. Hatneikim’s husband was injured, while the two other civilians who were with them remain missing.Thursday’s attack has taken the number of Kuki-Zo women killed in the Kuki-Naga clashes to 10, including two pregnant women. The clashes followed the Kuki-Meitei conflict that continued from 2023 to 2025.The attack came five days after nine people were killed across three districts, including two Kukis — one of them a woman — a Gorkha and six Naga men.Since the Kuki-Naga clashes began in Feb this year, at least 22 Naga and 32 Kuki-Zo people have been killed.Late on Wednesday night, security forces found the severed head of Naga man Ajinbou Ringkamai in Kangpokpi district.He was one of four Naga men killed when suspected Kuki militants attacked Makui Ashang village there on Oct 10. His head had been severed during the attack and remained missing. His headless body was taken to Jawaharlal Nehru Institute of Medical Sciences in Imphal on Oct 11.“The head was found in an isolated area near the site by security forces late on Wednesday night, and it was brought to JNIMS this morning for autopsy,” a senior official said.Joint Tribes Council Manipur, a Naga organisation, had given the authorities a 48-hour ultimatum to locate the head and ensure a proper funeral.Manipur home minister Govindas Konthoujam, speaking in Imphal on Thursday while visiting 84 BSF personnel admitted to Regional Institute of Medical Sciences with suspected food poisoning, said govt effort and security measures alone could not end the violence.“When the general people do not have humanity, then nobody can stop killing each other. We should understand that,” he said. “Killing will never solve any problem. We should talk to each other, and all differences should be resolved through dialogue.”He said govt was working to initiate dialogue but that society also had a role. “Security alone cannot solve the problem. We, the society and the people, should also try to restrain any kind of anger,” he said.Separately, Lt Gen Girish Kalia, General Officer Commanding of Spear Corps, visited an Assam Rifles forward post in Manipur on Thursday and reviewed the security situation. He was briefed on the preparedness of troops guarding India-Myanmar border.India shares a 1,643 km border with Myanmar, of which 398 km is in Manipur. Fencing has started, and nearly 55 km has been completed in the state. Govt plans to finish it by 2028. Hilly, forested terrain and resistance from militant outfits that use the border to move between the two countries are slowing the work.
Article Summary: A Kuki-Zo woman was killed and her husband injured in an alleged ambush by suspected Naga militants in Manipur’s Kamjong district. Two other members of the community were reported missing as ethnic violence continued in the state. The attack came five days after nine people were killed across three districts, including two Kukis and six Naga men.

Ukraine, European officials criticise deal

Kremlin accuses Kyiv of undermining peace efforts

Russian diesel has begun reaching global markets following an agreement with US President Donald Trump, the Kremlin said on Thursday, adding that the supplies could help stabilise oil markets but would not be sufficient to fully achieve that goal."The diesel has started reaching global markets and is expected to have a positive effect on stabilising oil markets, although it will not be enough to fully stabilize them," Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov told reporters, according to Reuters.Trump said last week that Russia had agreed to supply diesel to global markets to help lower fuel prices. Moscow subsequently partially lifted its ban on diesel exports from October 10 following the agreement.Data from financial information provider LSEG showed on Wednesday that Russia had resumed diesel export loadings from the Baltic port of Primorsk.According to the shipping data cited by Reuters, a tanker carrying around 40,000 metric tonnes of ultra-low sulphur diesel was loaded on October 13 and was heading towards Morocco.Trump said on Friday that Russia would immediately supply more than 300,000 metric tonnes, or 2.25 million barrels, of diesel to US and global markets.He also said another 500,000 tonnes would be supplied in November, followed by a further 1 million tonnes "immediately thereafter".However, the initial volume would amount to less than a day's supply for the US transport sector alone.US Energy Information Administration data puts daily consumption in the sector at around 2.94 million barrels. The additional volumes announced by Trump would amount to less than four days of demand for US transport.Trump is seeking to bring down US diesel prices ahead of the country's midterm elections on November 3.The agreement has drawn strong criticism from Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy, European officials and some Republican politicians in Trump's own party.Russia, meanwhile, has rejected European criticism of the diesel arrangement as "cynical", arguing that European countries continue to purchase some Russian oil and liquefied natural gas.The deal comes amid tensions over efforts to secure an energy ceasefire between Russia and Ukraine.Separately, the Kremlin said on Thursday that Ukrainian strikes on Russian oil refineries were running counter to US efforts to initiate peace talks, following a drone attack on a refinery in Russia's Ryazan region overnight.Peskov said Moscow did not believe Kyiv had complied with the energy ceasefire announced by Trump on Sunday. Ukraine had said it paused strikes on Russian oil refineries for three days but resumed them after Russia continued attacks on Ukrainian energy infrastructure."The Ukrainian regime in Kyiv continues to strike these facilities, thereby, of course, coming into serious contradiction with the peace efforts of the United States and of the American negotiators who are indeed making very vigorous efforts to somehow initiate the peace process. But so far, these vigorous attempts have been thwarted by the unwillingness of the Kyiv regime – and of (President Volodymyr) Zelenskyy personally – to make peace," Peskov said.The news agency Associated Press (AP) reported that the drone strike started a fire at the Ryazan refinery, around 300 kilometres southeast of Moscow. A senior Ukrainian official confirmed that Ukraine had hit the facility, while Russia's Defence Ministry and regional governor reported the attack.Russia had previously said the scope of the energy ceasefire had not been defined. On Wednesday, it said it had struck seven Ukrainian energy infrastructure facilities, according to Reuters.The competing claims over compliance with the ceasefire could not be independently verified.Meanwhile, Zelenskyy said Russia had launched more than 850 drones at Ukraine between midnight and Thursday morning.Ukraine's Emergency Services said three people were killed and six injured in a Russian drone attack on the central Kirovohrad region, while the Ukrainian Air Force said its air defences had intercepted 536 Russian drones during the overnight assault.
Article Summary: Russian diesel has begun reaching global markets following an agreement with US President Donald Trump, the Kremlin says. Trump said last week that Russia had agreed to supply diesel to global markets to help lower fuel prices. Moscow subsequently partially lifted its ban on diesel exports from October 10.

Article Title: Oil prices fall $1 after touching three week high amid Middle East tensions
Article Text:
Crude prices steady after touching three week high

Oil prices fell by more than $1 in early trade on Thursday as investors weighed threats to shipping through the Strait of Hormuz against the possibility of the US easing sanctions on oil-carrying vessels.Brent crude dropped 1.30% to $104.70, shedding $1.38, while West Texas Intermediate (WTI) fell 1.07% to $94.07, a decline of $1.02.The decline followed a sharp rise in WTI in the previous session, when prices reached a three-week high. The rally came after the Houthis attacked Saudi Aramco's headquarters and Iran announced new tactics to target vessels passing through the Strait of Hormuz, with the stated aim of keeping oil prices high.The threat to maritime traffic remained elevated. Two vessels: a container ship and a dry bulk carrier, sank near the strait within 24 hours after separate projectile strikes, maritime officials said on Wednesday.Attacks in the surrounding waters have increased over the past 10 days. Iran has said it is intensifying its strikes in retaliation for the US blockade of Iranian ports and the tougher sanctions imposed last month.The disruption caused by the Iran war has pushed freight costs to record highs, prompting the Trump administration to consider easing restrictions on vessels used to transport oil from sanctioned countries.A US official said on Wednesday that the administration was considering sanctions relief for so-called shadow fleet vessels, which have carried oil and petroleum products from countries including Russia, Iran and Venezuela. The move is aimed at helping reduce petroleum shipping costs.Furthermore, rising oil production and exports from Russia and the Middle East have also helped contain prices amid the supply concerns.Russia's crude oil output increased by 65,000 barrels per day in September to 8.43 million barrels per day, according to the International Energy Agency (IEA).However, production remained 870,000 barrels per day lower than a year earlier.The IEA also reported a monthly increase of 4.4 million barrels per day in crude oil exports from Middle East Gulf producers in September. Exports reached around 75% of their prewar levels.Now, the US-Iran conflict has continued for over seven months, keeping oil markets on edge. However, the price spike is far lower than the $126 per barrel levels seen earlier in the crisis.
Article Summary: Brent crude dropped 1.30% to $104.70, shedding $1.38, while West Texas Intermediate (WTI) fell 1.07%. The decline followed a sharp rise in WTI in the previous session, when prices reached a three-week high. The rally came after Iran announced new tactics to target vessels passing through the Strait of Hormuz.

Article Title: US stocks fall as inflation accelerates; S&P 500 drops 1.1%, Nasdaq slides 1.6%
Article Text:
Investors also weighed the risks and potential returns of heavy investment in artificial intelligence infrastructure.

Wall Street stocks fell on Wednesday as hotter-than-expected US inflation data pushed Treasury yields higher, adding to concerns about borrowing costs even as major banks assessed the opportunities and risks associated with the artificial intelligence (AI) investment boom.The S&P 500 fell 1.1%, putting it on track for its fifth decline in six sessions since hitting a record high. The Dow Jones Industrial Average dropped 171 points, or 0.3%, while the Nasdaq Composite declined 1.6%, as of 1:14 pm Eastern time.US consumer prices rose 3.7% year on year in September, accelerating from 3.4% in August and exceeding economists’ expectations of 3.6%. The data fuelled concerns that inflation could remain elevated, partly due to rising energy prices amid the war with Iran.The benchmark 10-year US Treasury yield climbed to 5.23%, after briefly crossing 5.32% during the session. Higher yields can weigh on equities by increasing borrowing costs and making bonds more attractive relative to stocks.Meanwhile, executives at major US banks highlighted the opportunities presented by AI infrastructure investment, while cautioning that uncertainty over demand, financing costs and returns could create risks.Goldman Sachs CEO David Solomon said the long-term demand for capital and computing capacity required by the AI ecosystem remained uncertain.“No one knows how the demands for capital and compute will evolve as the broader AI ecosystem matures,” Solomon said, stressing the need for vigilance in financing decisions and risk management.Citigroup CEO Jane Fraser, however, said investment in the broader AI ecosystem was not slowing, citing an ongoing shortage of computing capacity.The AI infrastructure expansion, driven by heavy investment in data centres and computing power, presents banks with opportunities to finance large-scale projects. However, elevated interest rates could raise project costs, squeeze returns and make debt repayment more difficult.Wells Fargo CEO Charlie Scharf described the AI buildout as a significant economic force, bringing both opportunities and risks because of the substantial borrowing involved and pressure on prices across some industries and supply chains.Banks are also deploying AI internally to improve productivity and reduce costs, although the financial benefits vary. Fraser said Citi was developing products up to 40% faster using AI and had reduced technology vendor expenses by 30% through coding tools.Investors are watching whether such efficiency gains can justify the heavy spending on AI. Concerns are also mounting over cybersecurity threats and the risks posed by AI agents capable of taking actions autonomously.The combination of persistent inflation, elevated bond yields and uncertainty over AI investment returns has added to the challenges facing Wall Street, where high stock valuations leave limited room for corporate earnings or productivity gains to disappoint.
Article Summary: US consumer prices rose 3.7% year on year in September, accelerating from 3.4% in August and exceeding economists’ expectations of 3.6%. The data fuelled concerns that inflation could remain elevated, partly due to rising energy prices amid the war with Iran. Investors also weighed the risks and potential returns of heavy investment in artificial intelligence infrastructure.

Article Title: US inflation accelerates to 3.7% in September as gasoline prices surge
Article Text:
This the sharpest increase in five months, as higher fuel costs and persistent underlying price pressures added to the cost-of-living burden

Gasoline prices drive inflation

Core inflation also picks up

What it means for Federal Reserve

US consumer inflation accelerated in September as a surge in gasoline prices and firmer underlying price pressures added to the cost-of-living burden for American households ahead of the November 3 midterm elections.The consumer price index (CPI) rose 3.7 per cent year-on-year in September, up from 3.4 per cent in August, the US Labor Department said on Wednesday. On a monthly basis, consumer prices increased 0.6 per cent, compared with a 0.4 per cent rise in the previous month.The annual inflation rate was slightly above economists' expectations of 3.6 per cent, according to a Reuters poll, while the monthly increase was in line with forecasts.The latest figures reflect the impact of higher energy costs following the US-Israeli war with Iran, which began in late February and disrupted oil and gas supplies. Rising costs have added to concerns over affordability, a key issue ahead of the midterm elections, in which President Donald Trump's Republican Party is seeking to retain control of Congress.Gasoline prices were a major contributor to the monthly increase in consumer prices, rising sharply in September.US Energy Information Administration data showed gasoline prices climbed 7.1 per cent during the month, while the Labor Department's CPI report recorded a 9.1 per cent increase.Higher fuel costs have also pushed up expenses across other sectors, including transportation and travel. Airfares rose 1.2 per cent in September and were up around 22 per cent from a year earlier, while hotel prices increased 2 per cent over the month.Rising fuel and transportation expenses have also increased costs for businesses, raising the risk that companies will pass some of the additional burden on to consumers through higher prices for goods and services.Grocery prices offered some relief, declining 0.1 per cent in September, although they remained 1.8 per cent higher than a year earlier.Underlying price pressures remained firm even after excluding volatile food and energy components.
